newsitem.title: UK: Emerging debt nudged higher on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Emerging debt nudged higher on short-covering.

text.p: Trading in emerging market debt continued sluggish in Europe on Wednesday as players awaited key U.S. data later this week.
"The market is almost dead. The big thing obviously is Friday. Nobody is making any big bets before then," a bond trader at a U.S. bank said. U.S. retail sales and producer price data are due Friday.
Short-covering accounted for most of what activity there had been, he added. That demand, particularly from local traders, helped Russian MinFins a little higher.
Russian MinFin 03 RU3E99=RR paper was quoted up 0.25 point at 84.75 bid, while the 05 RU3E08=RR added 0.125 point to 41.625 bid.
Russian President Boris Yeltsin will take two weeks vacation after his visit to Germany from April 16-18, the presidential press service said.

A Kremlin spokesman said Yeltsin would travel to the Black Sea resort of Sochi. Yeltsin, sidelined with heart problems and then pneumonia for most of the second half of last year and for some of this year, has often visited Sochi in the spring.
Elsewhere, there was interest in long-dated Latam sovereign paper. Argentina's ARGLB17=RR due 2017 added 0.25 point to 103.625 bid while Mexico's 30-year MXUMS=RR rose 0.75 point to 104.50.
Financial markets generally remain edgy about the prospects for U.S. inflation and interest rates.
